issue: Payment is due within 60 days of receipt of a valid, undisputed invoice rather than the preferred 45 days, which delays cash recovery for the Customer; no approval is required but the deviation must be tracked.
suggested_fix: The Customer shall pay valid, undisputed invoices within forty-five (45) days of receipt.

issue: The Agreement provides for service credits and a right to terminate for repeated Service Level failures, which meets the preferred position in structure, but the quantum of service credits and the designation of critical Service Levels are deferred entirely to each Statement of Work; until those SOWs are executed the fallback cap of 10% of monthly fees is not confirmed, leaving the Customer's remedy exposure undefined.
suggested_fix: If the Provider fails to meet a Service Level, the Provider shall credit the Customer with the service credits specified in the Statement of Work, which shall in no event be less than [●]% of the monthly Fees for the affected Service for each month in which the failure occurs, up to a maximum of ten percent (10%) of the monthly Fees for that Service.

issue: Clause 10 substantively meets the preferred data-protection position (DPDP Act 2023, GDPR where applicable, 72-hour breach notice, no cross-border transfer without safeguards), but the DPA on the Customer's standard template has not yet been executed; the rule requires Compliance escalation whenever there is any deviation from the preferred position, and the absence of a signed DPA means the preferred position is not yet fully achieved. The request form says no personal data is shared or processed. Check that with the requester before treating this as a gap.
suggested_fix: Attach the Customer's standard data processing agreement as Schedule [●] to this Agreement, executed by both Parties simultaneously with this Agreement, so that it takes effect on the Effective Date and no Personal Data is processed before it is in place.

issue: The contract requires payment within 60 days of receipt of a valid, undisputed invoice. The playbook preferred position is 45 days; 60 days is the fallback, which is only acceptable if the Provider accepts milestone payments tied to acceptance. No milestone-payment linkage is confirmed in the MSA body, so this sits at the fallback position and must be tracked.
suggested_fix: The Customer shall pay valid, undisputed invoices within forty-five (45) days of receipt.

issue: Service credits are capped at 10% of monthly fees (matching the fallback cap) and a termination right for repeated SLA failure exists; however, the contract does not itself set any minimum service-credit percentage — it defers the minimum to the Statement of Work, which is not supplied. The termination right for a single critical-SLA miss is also conditioned on the SOW designating a level as 'critical'. Because the operative credit floor and critical-SLA designation are entirely in an unseen SOW, the fallback position cannot be confirmed from the supplied document alone.
suggested_fix: which shall in no event be less than [●]% of the monthly Fees for the affected Service for each month in which the failure occurs, up to a maximum of ten percent (10%) of the monthly Fees for that Service.

issue: The contract requires the Customer to pay valid, undisputed invoices within 30 days of receipt, which is 15 days shorter than the preferred 45-day payment window. A shorter payment period reduces the Customer's cash-flow leverage and favours the Provider; no approval escalation is required under the playbook for this rule, but the deviation should be tracked.
suggested_fix: The Customer shall pay valid, undisputed invoices within 45 days of receipt.

issue: The liability cap carve-outs in Clause 13.3 exclude confidentiality (Clause 9), data protection (Clause 10), the Provider's indemnification obligations (Clause 12), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, and fraud — but do not explicitly carve out IP indemnity as a standalone category. The playbook requires the cap not to apply to 'indemnities' broadly; while Clause 12 (indemnification) is carved out in Clause 13.3(b), the playbook also specifically calls out 'IP indemnity' as a named carve-out. The current drafting covers it indirectly via the Clause 12 carve-out, creating potential ambiguity if a court reads 13.3(b) narrowly. No prohibited language ('unlimited liability') is present. The cap itself (12-month fees) matches the preferred position. This is a medium-confidence ambiguity requiring Legal Counsel review.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 13.3(b) to read: '(b) the Provider's indemnification obligations under Clause 12, including without limitation any indemnity for infringement of third-party Intellectual Property Rights;'

issue: Clause 5.3 provides for service credits and Clause 5.4 provides a termination right for repeated Service Level failures, which meets the preferred position on the face of the MSA. However, both provisions are conditional on service credits and Service Levels being 'specified in the Statement of Work'. If any SOW is silent on service credit amounts or does not designate a Service Level as 'critical', the Customer has no contractual remedy short of termination for material breach. The MSA itself contains no floor or default credit rate, meaning the fallback position (service credits capped at 10% of monthly fees) is not guaranteed. This creates a bounded but meaningful gap that should be tracked.
suggested_fix: Add a default service credit provision to Clause 5.3: 'If the applicable Statement of Work does not specify service credits for a particular Service Level failure, the Provider shall credit the Customer with an amount equal to five percent (5%) of the monthly Fees attributable to the affected Service for each month in which the failure occurs, up to a maximum of ten percent (10%) of the monthly Fees for that Service.'

issue: The liability cap in Clause 13.1 is measured against 'the total Fees paid or payable under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim.' For a contract with a USD 1,000,000 ceiling and a one-year term, this is functionally equivalent to the total contract value rather than a rolling 12-month slice of fees actually paid, which could expose the Customer to a higher cap than intended if fees are front-loaded or the contract is extended. The cap structure meets the preferred position in form but the 'total Fees paid or payable under this Agreement' language could be read to include all fees payable for the full term rather than only those paid or payable in the preceding 12 months. The clause does not contain the prohibited phrase 'unlimited liability' and carve-outs are present and correct. Position is assessed as fallback given the ambiguity in the cap measure. Legal Counsel approval is required.
suggested_fix: each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), breach of statutory duty or otherwise, shall not exceed the total Fees actually paid by the Customer to the Provider in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the date of the event giving rise to the claim.

issue: Clause 5 establishes the service-level framework (measurement, reporting, service credits, and termination for repeated failure) but the actual Service Levels and the quantum of service credits are entirely deferred to each Statement of Work. If any SOW is executed without a service-level schedule, the Customer has no measurable remedy short of termination. The fallback position requires service credits capped at 10% of monthly fees; no such cap or floor is set in the MSA itself. This is a bounded but meaningful gap that should be tracked.
suggested_fix: Insert a new Clause 5.5: 'Where a Statement of Work does not specify service credits, the Provider shall credit the Customer with an amount equal to five percent (5%) of the monthly Fees attributable to the affected Service for each month in which a Service Level is missed, up to a maximum of ten percent (10%) of the monthly Fees for that Service in any calendar month.'

issue: Clause 14.1 requires the Provider to maintain commercial general liability and professional indemnity insurance 'with limits of cover appropriate to the Services and not less than any amounts specified in a Statement of Work.' No minimum monetary amounts are stated in the MSA itself, and if no SOW specifies amounts, the Provider's self-assessed 'appropriate' level may be inadequate to back its indemnities. This is an administrative gap with limited but real substantive effect.
suggested_fix: each with limits of cover of not less than USD 2,000,000 per occurrence and USD 5,000,000 in aggregate (or such higher amounts as are specified in a Statement of Work), and in any event appropriate to the nature and scale of the Services.

issue: The agreement term is 2 years, which is the playbook's minimum fallback floor rather than the preferred 3-year term; this reduces the period during which the full suite of contractual protections (not just confidentiality survival) applies, and should be tracked as a fallback acceptance.
suggested_fix: This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for a period of three (3) years from the Effective Date, unless earlier terminated by either Party on thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Party.

issue: The agreement term is 2 years, which is the playbook's minimum fallback floor rather than the preferred 3-year term; this reduces the period during which active confidentiality obligations apply and favours Initech Software Ltd as the counterparty. No approval escalation is required but the deviation should be tracked.
suggested_fix: This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for a period of three (3) years from the Effective Date, unless earlier terminated by either Party on thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Party.

issue: The Services description in Clause 4.2 contains only the placeholder text 'This is for a test', with no named services, activities, or owners. Only one Deliverable (D1) is listed. If additional services or deliverables are intended, they are entirely undefined, creating dispute and overrun risk. Senior counsel should confirm whether the scope is genuinely limited to D1 or whether the contract was executed with incomplete scope language.
suggested_fix: [Insert a precise description of each Service the Provider is required to perform, including the activities, methodology, and any dependencies. Each Service should be linked to the Deliverable(s) it supports as listed in Clause 4.3.]

issue: Clause 8.1 states the pricing model is time-and-materials with a not-to-exceed cap, but Clause 8.2 simultaneously describes a fixed fee of INR 10,000,000.00 'inclusive of all Provider costs'. Both models are present in the same SOW with no mechanism to determine which applies, creating budget and billing uncertainty. This inconsistency requires Finance approval and resolution before execution.
suggested_fix:
8.1 Pricing model: Time and materials. The Fees for this SOW are charged on a time-and-materials basis under Clause 8.3 and may not exceed the not-to-exceed amount stated there.

8.2 [Deleted. This SOW is priced on a time-and-materials basis as stated in Clause 8.1. No fixed-fee arrangement applies.]

issue: The Services description in Clause 4.2 contains only placeholder text ('This is a test') with no named services, activities, or owners, creating a vague scope that is the primary cause of disputes and overruns; escalation to Legal Counsel is recommended before execution.
suggested_fix: 4.2 Services. The Provider shall perform the following Services: [INSERT: a complete, itemised description of each service to be performed, including the activity name, responsible Provider personnel, and any applicable due date or milestone linkage. Each service must be sufficiently described so that any service not listed is unambiguously out of scope under Clause 4.4.]

issue: The SOW is priced as a fixed fee (Clause 8.1 and 8.2) and includes a not-to-exceed cap and master-agreement rate references (Clause 8.4), which meets the preferred position; however, Clause 8.3 contains a fully operative time-and-materials sub-clause with its own not-to-exceed amount of INR 10,000,000.00, creating ambiguity as to which pricing model governs and potentially exposing the Customer to dual-track billing obligations. Finance approval is required given the ambiguity.
suggested_fix: Delete Clause 8.3 in its entirety, as this SOW is priced on a fixed-fee basis per Clause 8.1. If time-and-materials pricing is intended to apply to any portion of the Services, insert a separate, clearly scoped sub-clause identifying the specific services subject to time-and-materials rates, the applicable rate card reference, and the not-to-exceed amount for that portion only.
